nd0cc73b03ef.s: How many Telugu inscriptions of the Renati Cholas, mostly donation records, are known?
nd0cc73b03ef.x: Thirty-three Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions are known, most of them donation records (dana sasanalu).

na95d518cbb9.s: The Renati Cholas gave Telugu its first royal dignity about how many centuries before Nannaya?
na95d518cbb9.x: By using Telugu in royal and legislative records, the Renati Cholas gave it royal dignity about five centuries before Nannaya. (A match could not be built honestly from this single fact, so it is a one-liner.)

naad48c36a88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the emergence of Deccan dynasties?
o: The Gajapatis emerged before the Bahmanis.
naad48c36a88.x: The Gajapatis emerged in 1435, well after the Bahmani kingdom (1347); the other three dates are correct.

ne92a470e3af.s: The Bahmani kingdom split into the five Deccan Sultanates after the execution of Mahmud Gawan in:
ne92a470e3af.x: Mahmud Gawan was executed in 1482, after which the Bahmani kingdom split into five Deccan Sultanates; 1574 is when Ahmadnagar annexed Berar.

n463e0e414b0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the overlords of the Kota chiefs?
o: They were first subordinate to the Chalukya-Cholas.
The Velanati Chodas followed the Chalukya-Cholas as their overlords.
The Kakatiyas were their final overlords.
The Kakatiyas were their first overlords.
n463e0e414b0.x: The Kota chiefs served the Chalukya-Cholas first, then the Velanati Chodas and finally the Kakatiyas, so the Kakatiyas were the last, not the first, overlords.

n37be452eeab.s: In the Palnadu war, Brahmanaidu led the faction of:
n37be452eeab.x: Brahmanaidu led the Malideva faction; Nagamma was the minister on Nalagamaraju's side and opposed his reforms.

new.s: The Renati Cholas were first feudatories of the:
new.x: The Renati Cholas were first feudatories of the Pallavas and later of the Badami Chalukyas; the Eastern Chalukyas only copied their Telugu inscription style.

new.s: Renadu, the Renati Chola territory, was called 'Saptasahasra' because it had about how many villages?
new.x: Renadu was known as Saptasahasra, the land of 7,000 villages.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Renati Cholas:
1. Renadu lay where the Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor regions meet.
2. Renadu lay in the upper Pennar basin.
3. Dhanunjaya Varma ruled from Peddachapalli.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Renadu lay in the upper Pennar basin where Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor meet; Dhanunjaya Varma's capital was Chimbapuram, while Peddachapalli was the principal capital.

new.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Renati Chola dynasty?
new.x: Dhanunjaya Varma, son of Nandivarma, was the founder; Nandivarma was only the progenitor.

new.s: Which Renati Chola ruler bore the title 'Chola Maharaja'?
new.x: Satyaditya bore the title Chola Maharaja (Chola Mahadhiraju); the decline of the dynasty began after him.

new.s: Who was the last ruler of the Renati Cholas?
new.x: Elachola Maharaja was the last Renati Chola ruler.

new.s: The title 'Muditha Silakshara Navarama' belonged to:
new.x: Mahendra Vikramavarman, grandson of Nandivarma and father of Punyakumara, bore this title.

new.s: Punyakumara, the greatest Renati Chola ruler, ruled during:
new.x: Punyakumara ruled from 625 to 650 CE.

new.s: The Malepadu plates of Punyakumara, now in the Madras Museum, are written in:
new.x: The Malepadu plates of Punyakumara are in Sanskrit prose, unlike the Telugu Kalamalla record.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Renati Chola inscriptions?
o: The Kalamalla inscription is dated 575 CE.
The Malepadu plates belong to Punyakumara.
The Erragudipadu record is the first Telugu inscription of 575 CE.
The Kalamalla inscription was issued by Dhanunjaya Varma.
new.x: The 575 CE first Telugu inscription is Kalamalla; Erragudipadu is a separate late-6th-century stone record of Erikal Mutturaju.

new.s: By making Telugu a royal and legal language, the Renati Cholas replaced which languages in records?
new.x: The Renati Cholas were the first to make Telugu a royal and legal language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit.

new.s: The Erragudipadu inscription of the Renati Cholas was issued by:
new.x: The Erragudipadu stone record in Kamalapuram taluk belongs to Erikal Mutturaju, with a script like that of Kalamalla.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The Konidena Chodas ruled Kammanadu from Konidena near Narasaraopet; Pottapi was in Kadapa and Vikrama Simhapuri was the Nellore Choda seat.

new.s: The Pottapi Chodas of Kadapa originally came from:
new.x: The Pottapi Chodas came from Madhurantaka and were vassals of Chola Parantaka.

new.s: Nellore Choda Manumasiddhi II sought Kakatiya Ganapati's help against:
new.x: Manumasiddhi II sought the help of Kakatiya Ganapati against Vijayaganda Gopala.

new.s: Who was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas?
new.x: Bijjana was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas; Manumasiddhi I was their first king.

new.s: The Velamas (Recherla) ruled from:
new.x: The Recherla Velamas, founded by Singama, ruled from Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

new.s: The city of Hyderabad was founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in:
new.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad city in 1591; Sultan Quli founded the Golconda state in 1518 and the Charminar dates to 1594.

new.s: Who founded the Golconda (Hyderabad) state in 1518?
new.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah founded the Golconda state in 1518 (Nizami Mosque inscription); Muhammad Quli founded Hyderabad city.

new.s: Which dynasty came immediately after the Kakatiyas in the order of Andhra dynasties?
new.x: The Reddis (from 1325) came after the Kakatiyas, not before them.

new.s: The Kakatiya capital shifted from:
new.x: The Kakatiyas ruled first from Hanamkonda and then from Orugallu (Warangal).

new.s: Who captured Kakatiya Prataparudra in 1323?
new.x: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughlaq), sent by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, captured Prataparudra in 1323; Malik Kafur only made him a tributary.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi Sultanate invasions of Andhra:
1. Malik Kafur's campaign of 1309-10 made Prataparudra a tributary.
2. After 1323, Warangal was renamed Sultanpur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Malik Kafur made Prataparudra a tributary in 1309-10, and after Ulugh Khan's conquest of 1323 Warangal was renamed Sultanpur.

new.s: Before becoming sovereign in 1163, the Kakatiyas were feudatories first of the:
new.x: The Kakatiyas served the Rashtrakutas and then the Kalyani Chalukyas before Rudradeva declared independence in 1163.

new.s: The Kota family, local rulers of Dharanikota, was subordinate to the:
new.x: The Kota family was a Kakatiya subordinate and married Ganapatideva's daughter Ganapamba, not a Gajapati vassal.

new.s: Before becoming independent in 1518, the Qutb Shahi founder was the Bahmani tarafdar of:
new.x: Sultan Quli was the Bahmani tarafdar of Telangana (1496) before becoming independent in 1518.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT among the contenders for the Krishna-Godavari doab and coastal Andhra?
new.x: The coastal dispute was among the Reddis, Velamas, Gajapatis, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis; the Imad Shahis ruled Berar.

new.s: In the Battle of Bhimavaram (1368), Kapaya Nayaka was killed by the:
new.x: At Bhimavaram in 1368 the Recherla Velamas killed Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka and gained Telangana.

new.s: The sieges of Kondavidu and Kondapalli (1515-16) were fought between Krishnadevaraya and the:
new.x: Krishnadevaraya besieged Kondavidu and Kondapalli in 1515-16 against the Gajapatis.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: At Raichur in 1520 Krishnadevaraya defeated the Adil Shah of Bijapur; Muttukur was Ganapatideva vs Pandyas and Bhimavaram was Velamas vs Kapaya Nayaka.

new.s: Which of the following did NOT join the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565)?
new.x: Golconda, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Bidar fought Vijayanagara at Talikota; Berar did not join.

new.s: Berar was annexed in 1574 by:
new.x: Berar, ruled by the Imad Shahis, was annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.

new.s: How many sultans ruled the Qutb Shahi state (1518-1687)?
new.x: The Qutb Shahi state lasted from 1518 to 1687 under seven sultans.

new.s: In Rayalaseema, the Kakatiyas (through their Kayastha chiefs) were succeeded by:
new.x: The Rayalaseema sequence is Kakatiyas (Kayastha chiefs) → Vijayanagara → Qutb Shahis.

new.s: In Telangana, the rule of the Delhi Sultanate (1323) was followed by the:
new.x: The Telangana sequence is Kakatiyas → Delhi Sultanate (1323) → Musunuri Nayakas → Velamas / Bahmanis → Qutb Shahis.

new.s: Who was the first Chalukya-Chola king?
new.x: Kulottunga I (Rajendra Chalukya) was the first Chalukya-Chola king (APPSC 2011).

new.s: The Chalukya-Chola viceroys of Vengi assumed the Eastern Chalukya titles:
new.x: The viceroys of Vengi took the Eastern Chalukya titles Sarvalokasraya and Sri Vishnuvardhana.

new.s: Kulottunga I took Vengi in 1075 after the death of the last Eastern Chalukya:
new.x: Kulottunga I took Vengi in 1075 after the death of Vijayaditya VII, the last Eastern Chalukya.

new.s: Vikrama Chola was recalled from Vengi in 1118 to become his father's:
new.x: Vikrama Chola, son of Kulottunga I, was recalled in 1118 to be his father's co-regent.

new.s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send to China?
new.x: Kulottunga I sent a mission of 72 merchants to China.

new.s: The Palnadu Haihayas ruled from:
new.x: The Palnadu Haihayas ruled from Gurajala; Rakuduru was the Kona Haihaya capital.

new.s: The Chagis ruled the Natavadi and Vijayavati vishayas from:
new.x: The Chagis, raised to Mandaleswara rank by Kulottunga I, ruled from Gudimetta (later also Vinukonda).

new.s: The ancestors of the Velanati Chodas were the:
new.x: The Velanati Chodas were not related to the Telugu Chodas; their ancestors were the Kirtipura lords of Madhyadesha.

new.s: The capital of the Velanati Chodas was:
new.x: The Velanati Chodas ruled from Chandavolu (Dhanadapuram); founder Gonka I, greatest Gonka II.

new.s: Which Kota ruler (1108-1127) led Kalinga campaigns with the Velanati Chodas?
new.x: Kota Bhimaraju I (1108-1127) backed the Chalukya-Cholas and joined the Velanati Chodas in Kalinga campaigns.

new.s: The overlords of the Chagi chiefs, in order, were:
new.x: The Chagis served the Chalukya-Cholas, then the Kakatiyas, then the Gajapatis; the Velanati stage belongs to the Kota chiefs.

new.s: Nalagamaraju was the son of Mailama Devi, daughter of Velanati:
new.x: Nalagamaraju's mother Mailama Devi was the daughter of Velanati Gonka II.

new.s: The rival factions of the Palnadu war were all sons of the Palnadu Haihaya ruler:
new.x: Both factions were sons of Palnadu Haihaya Alugaraju (Anugaraju); Malideva and his brothers were Nalagamaraju's half-brothers.

new.s: The Pusapati family had its seat at:
new.x: The Pusapatis ruled from Vizianagaram (APPSC GS 2022); Peddapuram was the seat of the Vatsavayis.

new.s: Raja Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram was killed fighting the East India Company in the Battle of:
new.x: Vijayarama Raju was killed at the Battle of Padmanabham on 10 July 1794, after which Vizianagaram became a tributary zamindari.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pusapatis and Vatsavayis:
1. Vizianagaram was settled as a zamindari estate under the Permanent Settlement of 1802.
2. The Vatsavayis had their seat at Peddapuram.
3. The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1802.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vizianagaram became a zamindari estate in 1802 and the Vatsavayis ruled from Peddapuram; the Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.

new.s: The Matsyas of Oddadi claimed descent from a:
new.x: The founder of the Matsyas of Oddadi claimed descent from a fish (matsya); their emblem was a double fish.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Matsyas of Oddadi:
1. Their founder Satyamartanda married Prabhavati, daughter of the king of Utkala.
2. Oddadi lies about 16 miles from Anakapalle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Satyamartanda married Prabhavati, daughter of Jayatsena of Utkala, who made him ruler of Oddadi, which lies about 16 miles from Anakapalle.

new.s: The Satrasala inscription is the founder's record of:
new.x: The Satrasala inscription belongs to Betaraju I, founder of the Palnadu Haihaya line at Gurajala.

new.s: The Taruvariyur inscription praises which ruler as a thunderbolt to his enemies?
new.x: The Taruvariyur inscription praises Nellore Choda Manumasiddi I as a thunderbolt to his enemies.
